stem: A nurse is caring for an adult client with an intellectual disability. A family member begins answering every question for the client. Which communication approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Communicate clearly and directly with the client, adapting the communication method as needed rather than automatically directing all questions to the family member.
options.B: Direct all communication to the family because an intellectual disability means the client cannot participate.
options.C: Use the same fixed communication method for every person with an intellectual disability.
options.D: Avoid asking the client questions because additional time for communication is not clinically useful.

rationale: CDC guidance for healthcare providers recommends effective communication with patients who have intellectual disabilities, including communicating clearly and directly with the patient, repeating or rephrasing information or using another method when needed, and taking the time required to meet the patient's healthcare needs. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Use respectful, individualized, direct communication with an adult client who has an intellectual disability.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Disability and Health Information for Healthcare Providers
source_locator: What healthcare providers can do — communicate clearly and directly with the patient; adapt wording/method if needed; take the time needed; overview explicitly includes intellectual disability
source_claim_supported: Healthcare providers should communicate effectively with patients with intellectual disabilities, communicate clearly and directly with the patient, adapt communication when needed, and allow adequate time.
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — therapeutic communication, dignity and individualized psychosocial care
blueprint_topic: Communication with clients with intellectual disabilities
correction_summary: Replaced the insufficient NICHD overview source with current CDC healthcare-provider guidance that directly supports the communication claim. Removed broad unsupported autonomy/capacity language and focused on direct, respectful, individualized communication. Reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
audit_findings: CDC explicitly includes intellectual disability and directs providers to communicate clearly and directly with the patient and adapt communication as needed. A is uniquely correct; B-D make unsupported assumptions or obstruct effective communication. Independent second pass passed.
